newsitem.title: USA: UPS strike poses some problems in region - NY NAPM.
newsitem.headline: UPS strike poses some problems in region - NY NAPM.

text.p: Twenty-one percent of New York-area purchasing managers have experienced "severe" or "very severe" purchasing and delivery problems because of the United Parcel Service strike, a survey showed.

Nearly 80 percent of respondents, however, described the strike impact as moderate to slight, said the National Association of Purchasing Management - New York (NAPM-NY), the group that sponsored the survey.
Of the managers reporting UPS-related difficulties, 8.0 percent cited a backup in inventories to be shipped, while 29 percent said they were experiencing shortages.
"This finding more heavily reflected the service-sector base of the New York region, which tends to be more of a user than a supplier of goods," NAPM-NY said.
Purchasing managers reported a median delay of two to three days.
Two-thirds of purchasers who said they had switched to package carriers other than UPS reported higher shipping costs, while the rest said costs had remained about the same.
The survey was conducted on August 12 and 13. NAPM-NY did not say how many purchasers were polled.
